measurement_semantics.wall: Whole CLI command including cleanup; helper overhead and timing-external host observations excluded.
measurement_semantics.cpu: wait4 user and system CPU counters for the command and its children; separate from elapsed scope sums.
measurement_semantics.memory: wait4 maximum resident-set counter for the command and its children; not CLI-only RSS or a simultaneous process-tree memory sum.
measurement_semantics.workers: Automatic upper bound, not an observed concurrent worker count.
measurement_semantics.cache_and_host_load: Uncontrolled; full native batch has one pause; short batches proceed under recorded host load.

baseline_source_binding.method: Retrospective full-tree source census, recovered original build invocation, and retained binary identity.
limits: Source census and file timestamp checks were collected retrospectively.
Binding relies on retained filesystem metadata and build artifacts.
This is not a build-time clean-tree log or a fully isolated rebuild.
The native batch has one between-case pause.
Cache and host load remain uncontrolled across the pause.
The original interrupted summary is preserved; it is not reported as a complete continuous batch.
Host load is recorded before and after commands without waiting for a quiet host.
Observer errors are missing observations, not failed media verification or zero background work.
Snapshots are outside CLI elapsed time and describe observed host load.
Missing or partial process observations do not establish zero background work.
Process-CPU percentage sums are ps observations, not interval CPU utilization or precise peaks.
Classified counts omit the observer and ancestors; all-process CPU sums include all observed rows.
The host is not isolated; timing differences are descriptive observations under recorded load.

Compare builds only within the same source, recipe and verification depth.
Full-input native and excerpt decoded timings are different workloads and media sizes.
Native and complete-decoding depths perform different verification work.
Mixed and stitch-both recipes perform different boundary work.
The entire selected asset is checked at its requested depth; the excerpt is a distinct input.

source_correspondence.changed_crate_files_scope: External integration test only; no release CLI production source changes.

selected_helper_diagnostics.scope: Selected single-threaded parser and reader helpers over synthetic bytes; not a complete CLI or MP4 measurement.

semantic_controls.checksum_kind: Full-output traversal using a noncryptographic FNV-style 64-bit checksum; not SHA-256 or bytewise equality proof.

limits: No timing or whole-CLI allocation, MP4/cryptographic pipeline, or maximum-open-files claim.
Warm buffer allocation and destruction are outside the measured interval; retained warm storage is not included in interval live/peak requested bytes.
GlobalAlloc entries describe requested bytes, not allocator rounding, physical memory, internal realloc copying or transient storage.
Copy and zeroize counters describe logical operation target bytes; repeated wipes count repeatedly, including Vec capacity on drop.
Kernel deltas are same-process Unix and Mach syscall totals, not read/lseek classes or child-process I/O.
Empty-control Unix/Mach totals are preserved without subtraction; observation overhead remains.
These synthetic helper checks are separate from actual media source, packet, timing, manifest and decoded-content verification.
